title: Harfuch: Third Suspect Detained in Ojocaliente Car Bomb, ~200kg of Explosives Used, CJNG–Cártel del Pacífico Turf Dispute a Lead Theory
detail: On September 4, 2026, Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch, speaking from Zacatecas at the federal government's morning press briefing, disclosed new details on the August 30 Ojocaliente car bomb investigation. Harfuch said ministerial proceedings indicate the vehicle carried approximately 200 kilograms of explosive material, and that authorities now have three detainees: Juan Pedro 'N' (previously reported detained; described as the alleged main person responsible for placing the device against state forces), and two additional suspects, Hipólito 'N' and Miguel 'N', both allegedly tied to a criminal cell operating between Aguascalientes and Zacatecas and accused of conducting surveillance ahead of the attack — Miguel 'N' also carries an outstanding arrest warrant for homicide. Harfuch said one principal investigative line links the bombing to a territorial dispute between cells of CJNG and the 'Cártel del Pacífico' (a reference to Sinaloa Cartel-aligned factions) over routes and illicit activity in Zacatecas, alongside the earlier retaliation theory tied to prior arrests. He stressed the investigation was not concluded and extends to possible responsible parties operating outside Zacatecas.

media.caption: Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch briefs on the Ojocaliente, Zacatecas car bomb investigation

confidenceReason: The additional detainee count and explosives estimate come directly from the federal Security Secretary at an official briefing and are corroborated by two independent Tier-2 outlets; the CJNG–Cártel del Pacífico dispute is explicitly framed by Harfuch as one investigative line among others, not a concluded finding.
